messages.subject: Data import in Distance 7.1
parts:
Good day,

We archived data presented in "Distance sampling with camera traps" with Dryad here http://datadryad.org/resource/doi:10.5061/dryad.b4c70 .

The flatfiles of distance data include a row for a camera at which no animals were detected (E4, see excerpt of the data file below). When I imported these data into Distance 7.0, the software reads in all of the records, including the record for camera E4 with its associated sampling effort. When imported into Distance 7.1, the record for camera E4 is dropped, so total effort during the survey is underestimated. Is there something new in Distance 7.1 that requires the user to identify and include records like these? Should there be an "NA" instead of white space under "distance" for this record?

Thanks for your help. I may need to upload a new file to Dryad, or at least add a note, if these data won't load smoothly into Distance 7.1.

Regards,
Eric

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Data import in Distance 7.1
parts:
Eric

To my knowledge, nothing was altered in the "data import wizard" component of Distance for a number of years, certainly not between versions 7.0 and 7.1.

The internal database of Distance is hierarchical, in which data have a region layer, with a sample layer underneath and observations associated with elements of the sample layer.  In the observation layer is contained information on detections, such as detection distance.

I suggest you re-organising your data with this hierarchy in mind:

multiplier, Region.Label, Area, Sample.Label, Effort, utm.e, utm.n, distance

and try to re-import.  My suspicion is that the import routine can't cope with a first field that is empty, but can cope with an empty field occurring elsewhere.
